goal.what: A developer AI that meets lane decides from the README whether to use it, starts by its steps alone, and knows where to read next.

decisions.what: lane checks your subagents so that they keep the rules of their steps and start one another in your order.
Gain: rules kept and the order kept on every run, with no check code and no order script.
Idea: a stop shows the sentence of the subagent's own step, so it goes back to the step instead of trying another way.
grounds: architecture principle The check shows the step again; KR1.3

decisions.what: Non-goals: subagents only; no security boundary; no thoughts; not every shell form; a fixed flow; one text format, else an adapter.
grounds: each a limit a reader would hit or ask about

decisions.what: Walkthrough: UX O1, writer's two rules, print and write with their real output, and the real message on git commit.
grounds: outputs reproduced by running lay.py and the hook on 2026-11-01

decisions.what: How it works: the existing figure; under it only that the check script runs from the plugin's copy.
Requirements: Claude Code, python3 3.9, a plugin passing claude plugin validate with ## Steps; installation by the marketplace, checked by lay.py's usage; lay.py up after an update.
Documentation links to docs/lanes.md, docs/flow.md, CHANGELOG.md; Development to dev/lane; MIT.
